solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A piece about fine 17 member?

indicators.note: one thing set about another wraps around it, so the piece goes round the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a chess or draughts piece is a man
an eric was the blood-fine paid for a killing under old Irish law

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fine item belongs to a set of seventeen.
explanation.walkthrough: A + M(ERIC)AN. The eric is an obscure word from old Irish Brehon law; 17 is YANKEES, and the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a colloquial name for a person from the United States, so any American counts as one of the Yankees.

clue.text: Note bird sizzles right away in ovens

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is sent away, taken out of the word before it

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a crow is a black bird
something that sizzles is hot, a rave success
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cook notes that a bird is sizzling nicely in the ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: MI + CROW + RAVES with its R removed. 'Sizzles' here is the slang sense of being a hit, as raves are.
explanation.definitionFit: Microwaves are kitchen appliances that heat food, a modern kind of oven.

clue.text: Rigorous elder is involved in one of these groups?

definitions.text: Rigorous elder is involved in one of these groups?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters before it are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strict church elder is suspected of belonging to some devout society.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a rigorous elder could well be a member of such a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious orders are communities such as monks or nuns bound by vows, the kind of body a strict elder might join.

clue.text: Process engineering remains

indicators.note: engineering means building or rigging up, so the word before it is reconstructed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some industrial process, it turns out, still continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning dead bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Human remains are dead bodies, which is exactly what corpses are.

clue.text: Food hospital put out gets rejections

indicators.note: putting something out ejects it, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: nosh is slang for food
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Food sent back by the hospital earns refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSH with its H thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Noes are refusals, so rejections are a set of nos.

clue.text: No good justification for regular calls

indicators.note: 'no good' means the abbreviation for good is absent from the word that follows

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
grounds are a reason or justification

explanation.surface: Someone protests there is no real excuse for phoning so often.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUNDS without its G.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's or milkman's rounds are the regular series of visits made on a fixed circuit.

clue.text: Rover car about to drop off British author

indicators.note: dropping off means falling away, so the short word for about leaves the word car

blocks.note: taken as written
ca, short for circa, means about
Eric Ambler was a British writer of spy thrillers

explanation.surface: A Rover car is driven by a British writer about to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR loses CA, leaving R, then AMBLER. Rover with its capital looks like the British car make, but it is a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler wanders about without fixed purpose, as does a rover.

clue.text: Two separate articles in lingerie the worse for wear

indicators.note: in puts the articles inside the word for lingerie, at two separate points

blocks.note: the definite article, taken twice and placed apart
lingerie is women's underwear

explanation.surface: Two items of lingerie are looking rather tattered.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles go in at different points of the garment word, not side by side. 'Articles' looks like garments but means the grammatical word the.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the weather is an idiom for feeling unwell, just as the worse for wear means in poor shape.

clue.text: Does perhaps rush around…

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the plant is read backwards

blocks.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person perhaps hurries about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as the verb but is the plural of doe; 'perhaps' marks does as one example of the defined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Does are female deer, so deer covers them as an example of the class.

clue.text: Bidding system in pub briefly making a comeback

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is lopped off
coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A pub's auction scheme is enjoying a brief revival.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL shortened to LOCA, then reversed. Acol is the standard bidding system in British contract bridge, named after a club in Acol Road, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is a set of conventions for bidding at bridge, which is what a bidding system is.

clue.text: Pale pink kerosene coming out of Shell with more crackers

indicators.note: emerging from its shell means losing the outer letters, so only the inside of the fuel word is kept

blocks.note: the middle of this word, with the outer pairs stripped away
crackers means mad, so more crackers is madder

explanation.surface: A fuel blend from the Shell oil company has come out an odd pale pink, which seems even more crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell's capital points to the oil company, but here a shell is the outside of kerosene: remove KE and NE and ROSE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose madder is a pigment and colour from the madder plant, a pale pinkish red.

clue.text: Shout about new post eg for a fervent preacher

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters following it are given a fresh order
about means surrounding, so the word for shout goes round the mixed letters

blocks.note: to holler is to shout
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone shouts about a new job, say for an enthusiastic preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'eg' look like separate words in the surface but are simply six letters to mix; 'for a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-gospeller is an evangelist who preaches with zeal and fire, a fervent preacher.

clue.text: … making grannie uneasy

indicators.note: uneasy means unsettled, so the letters before it are disturbed into another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, a rushing deer is making granny nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join it to the previous clue in the surface only. 'Making' is used in the money sense, as in making a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To be earning is to be making money, as in making a good salary.

clue.text: Heard publican's role in basement bar

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the ear catches, not by the spelling

blocks.note: a publican's job is to sell beer

explanation.surface: A landlord's part in a cellar bar is overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: A publican is the landlord of a British pub, whose role is that of a beer seller; the sound is respelt as the drinking place.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer cellar is an underground drinking room, a bar in the basement.

clue.text: Credit squeezes create a stir in boozer

indicators.note: something that squeezes another holds it tightly inside, so the abbreviation wraps round the next phrase

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to arouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: Tight credit causes a row at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: C(AROUSE)R. 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, the misleading reading here; it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A carouser drinks heavily and noisily at parties, so is a boozer in the drinker sense.

clue.text: What shoe repairers do about list

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a ship that lists heels over, leaning to one side

explanation.surface: Cobblers explain what they do with a list of tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' is not an itemised record but the nautical verb for a ship leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheel shoes is to fit new heels, a standard job at a cobbler's.

clue.text: Jumper is indeed on back to front after a whiff of joint

indicators.note: a whiff is just a faint hint, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
back to front means turned round so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the first letter of joint
yes, indeed, as emphatic agreement
re means on, as in concerning

explanation.surface: Someone claims a jumper has been put on the wrong way round after a puff on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: J then YES + RE read backwards. A jumper is British English for a sweater, and a jersey is the same garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, which in British English is called a jumper.

clue.text: Code words on the radio for US baseball team

blocks.note: first meaning: the word used for the letter Y in the radio phonetic alphabet, in the plural
second meaning: the New York baseball club

explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO spelling alphabet used over radio, each letter has a code word, and Yankee stands for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio alphabet's term for Y in the plural, and the nickname of the famous New York Major League side.

clue.text: Anger about broadcasting battles – it's strong stuff

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for anger is placed round the next pieces

blocks.note: ire is anger
a programme that is broadcasting is on air
war is a state of battles between nations

explanation.surface: Fury over the televising of battles is strongly worded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' reads as a description of the battles, but it supplies the short word meaning on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironware means goods made of iron, a tough and strong material.

clue.text: Oscar's involved in business concern? The opposite

definitions.note: the opposite of 'involved', i.e. not involved

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it, so the letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O
an outfit is a firm or organisation

explanation.surface: Oscar is mixed up in some company; or is it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: OUT(O)FIT. 'The opposite' points back to the word involved, so the answer means not involved, left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out of it is to be excluded or left out, the reverse of being involved.

clue.text: Tries again with treaties gone wrong?

definitions.text: Tries again with treaties gone wrong?

indicators.note: wrong means out of order, so the letters before it are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Diplomats have another go when their treaties have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: when treaties go wrong, one makes another attempt at the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegotiate is to discuss terms again, the natural second attempt after an agreement breaks down.

clue.text: Fancy wife overlooking that man!

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means sitting above, so the first piece is placed on top

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
that man is him

explanation.surface: A wife ignoring her husband exclaims at the idea of fancying him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' suggests ignoring, but in a down answer it means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, in the sense of a sudden notion or impulse, is a whim.

clue.text: Disgruntled Labour scoffed about Ambassador East

indicators.note: to labour is to work, and worked letters are kneaded into another order
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the ambassador and the direction

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Fed-up Labour Party members mocked the ambassador from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with its capital looks like the British political party; it is the signal to rework scoffed, which then wraps HE and E after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for annoyed or fed up, the state of being disgruntled.

clue.text: Ugly creature appearing in exorcism

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters show up inside the next word, already in order

blocks.note: the second to fourth letters

explanation.surface: A hideous monster shows up during an exorcism.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a brutish goblin-like monster of fantasy fiction, notably Tolkien's.

clue.text: Leave miserable places, no end of trouble

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter that follows is taken out of the word for the places
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'trouble'

blocks.note: a hole is a dismal, squalid place
the last letter of trouble

explanation.surface: Get away from wretched places and the trouble is over.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLES without E. 'Leave' reads as a verb but is the noun for time off; hols is British informal for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Hols is British slang for holidays, which are leave from work.

clue.text: One discounted broadsheet is separating word parts

indicators.note: discounted means not counted, so the numeral for one is left out of the newspaper

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
The Times is a British broadsheet newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cut-price newspaper is splitting words apart.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMES loses I, then IS. Tmesis is the insertion of a word into another, as in abso-bloody-lutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Tmesis is the grammatical term for splitting a word by inserting another between its parts.

clue.text: Secretary mostly working for food suppliers

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped
working means in operation, so the letters are set going in a new order

blocks.note: the word without its final Y

explanation.surface: A secretary works mostly for the people who supply food.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterers provide food and drink for functions, so they are suppliers of food.
